text:
anya: quick design check-in  proposing an "escrow + probe" approach for smoothing tenant bursts so we avoid immediate 429s for short spikes. high level: tiny per-shard escrow, probes to admission for topups, gradual degrade when admission blocks.

maria.k: sounds promising. how small are escrows?

anya: base escrow = min(100 reqs, max(20, commit*0.01)). adjusted by recent burst MA. goal: local short spikes served without RPCs.

kevin: probes = extra QPS on admission. rate limit?

anya: yes, probe throttle: 1 probe/tenant/200ms for cold tenants, batched 20ms for hot tenants. payload tiny: tenant_id, escrow_left, probe_nonce. response: {ok|throttle, topup_amt, token}.

priya: abuse detection?

anya: two layers: simple heuristics (retry density, 429 spike, payload entropy) + a lightweight classifier at admission that flags coordinated fanout. in shadow for 2w then gated.

maria.k: rollout?

anya: plan: 1) sim historical traces 2) shadow probes 3) enable topups for 5% tenants 4) widen with metrics gates. revert via signed decision token invalidation.

kevin: edge change complexity? small state machine: escrow counter, probe scheduler, token cache.

priya: Dedicated/private?

anya: Dedicated gets local admission binary to optionally sync escrows. Private can opt-in to run admission locally. doc tradeoffs.

maria.k: ok please RFC + sim metrics (client 429, p50/p99, FP rate, admission QPS).

anya: will draft today. @deploy-bot please publish when ready.

deploy-bot: RFC draft published: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/1787654321-escrow-probe-flow (permissions: eng-infra, eng-platform)

kevin: ack, will prototype probe batching.

priya: i'll start dashboards for FP detection and escrow utilization.
